title: Which game is the most popular in their class?
description: A question from the book asks for the most popular game in the class of the two friends. The video fills a table with the count for each game, checks the counts against the number of children, and picks the largest.
teaching_notes: One idea: fill a table of counts, check that the counts add up to the number of children, then pick the largest. The check catches a child who was missed or counted twice.

source: Figure it Out: what is the most popular game in their class
video_script.why: The child counts every game from the book's list and picks the largest count.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own list of the favourite games of 31 children
video_script.anchor: the favourite-games list of Ziva and Laksh
video_script.payoff_line: Hockey is the most popular game, chosen by eight children.

names.Ziva: girl who makes the favourite-games list with Naresh
names.Laksh: boy who collects favourite games with Navya

maths_rules: Kabaddi 6, hockey 8, cricket 6, satoliya 5, football 4, badminton 2.
8 is the largest of the six counts.
video_script.design: One two-column table of six rows filled from the book's list, then a sum under it to check the total.

beats.on_screen: title card with the favourite-games list of thirty one children beside the two friends

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the list
marks.ask: a question mark lights up beside the list

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the class of Ziva and Laksh.
The list shows the favourite game of each of thirty one children.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the most popular game in their class?

beats.on_screen: the list and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the list with each game coloured, and an empty table of two columns beside it

marks.rows: the empty table appears with one row for each game
marks.count: an arrow runs from the list to the empty second column

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>A table gives one row to each game and keeps its count beside it.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The game with the largest count is the one most children chose.

beats.on_screen: Given: the list of 31 children and their favourite games

marks.given: the list is written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the list of thirty one children and their favourite games.

beats.on_screen: To find: the most popular game

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the most popular game in their class.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: table with the six games in the first column: Kabaddi, Hockey, Cricket, Satoliya, Football, Badminton

marks.games: the six game names appear in the first column

narration: <bookmark mark='games'/>Step one, write the six games in the first column of a table.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: Kabaddi 6, Hockey 8, Cricket 6, Satoliya 5, Football 4, Badminton 2 in the second column

marks.count: the list is read once for each game and the count is written in the second column
marks.rest: the last three counts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count the children for each game and fill the second column.
Kabaddi has six, hockey eight, and cricket six.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Satoliya has five, football four, and badminton two.

marks.add: the six counts are added in a line under the table

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add all six counts to check them.
Six plus eight plus six plus five plus four plus two is thirty one.
<bookmark mark='match'/>That matches the thirty one children, so no child was missed.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: find the largest count in the second column

marks.largest: the largest count in the second column is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='largest'/>Step four, look for the largest count. Eight is larger than all the others.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Hockey is the most popular game, chosen by 8 children
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Hockey is the most popular game, chosen by eight children.
